researchQuestion: Can aggregate and issuer-facing credit-supply conditions improve Taiwan stock selection after separating loan demand, policy rates and issuer fundamentals?
mechanism: Bank credit supply can tighten through lending standards, pricing, collateral, maturity or quantity even before defaults rise.
Bank-dependent firms may be more sensitive to credit-supply contractions than firms able to substitute into public bond/equity markets.
Bank-to-bond substitution can help identify credit-supply stress when external financing demand is positive.

evidenceAndCounterevidence.support: Research using lending standards finds credit-supply shocks affect loan growth and real activity.
evidenceAndCounterevidence.counter: Observed loan growth alone confounds demand and supply.

evidenceAndCounterevidence.support: Bank-to-bond substitution rises in episodes of tight standards, bank distress and monetary tightening in some evidence.
evidenceAndCounterevidence.counter: Bond issuance may reflect issuer quality/size selection and favorable market timing, not only bank stress.

evidenceAndCounterevidence.support: Corporate debt booms can precede weak future growth/crisis outcomes at macro level.
evidenceAndCounterevidence.counter: Macro credit-cycle evidence does not automatically provide issuer-level stock-selection alpha.

taiwanSourceRoute: Taiwan central-bank publications provide bank lending rates and credit aggregates; five-major-bank new-loan weighted-average rates are one aggregate financing-cost input.
Issuer-level loan approvals/standards are often non-public; missing bank-supply state remains UNKNOWN.
Policy/risk-free rate level is owned by D13; D22-11 owns incremental bank-credit availability/terms.
pitContract: Use release-date vintage for macro/bank data; later revisions never backfill.
Separate credit demand proxies from supply proxies before causal interpretation.
Map aggregate lending conditions to issuer exposure only with pre-known bank dependence/funding mix from D22-10.
Loan volume changes without standards/pricing/demand controls are context-only, not supply shocks.
Countrywide conditions cannot be mechanically converted into identical issuer scores.
falsificationGates: Falling loan growth != tighter supply by itself; demand may have collapsed.
Rising loan rates != issuer credit spread by itself; risk-free policy transmission belongs to D13.
Tight standards can coexist with strong bond markets, reducing effects for market-access firms.
Bank stress can be offset by government/central-bank facilities or alternative finance.
If issuer-level interaction adds no incremental information after D13 + D22-10 + fundamentals, classify REJECTED_OR_REDUNDANT.
next: Search for source-attested lending-standard, approval/rejection, collateral, maturity-term or natural-experiment evidence that can separate supply from demand.
Extend issuer bank-dependence PIT receipts from D22-10 funding states.
Treat CBC aggregate loan rates and enterprise funding surveys as CONTEXT_ONLY until supply identification is proven.
Keep D22-11 L2 unless the identification gate is satisfied; do not infer supply shocks from loan growth or rates alone.

maturityDecision.reason: Release-vintage Taiwan bank-pricing and enterprise-funding context plus issuer bank-dependence exposure are replayable, but the distinctive bank-credit-supply shock cannot yet be separated from borrower demand using public modern Taiwan data. Promoting on loan rate/volume alone would violate the module's own falsification gate.
